XXVII.}}</noinclude>''them: and vpon my vesture they did cast lottes''. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=36}}† And they sate and vvatched him. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=37}}† And they put ouer his head his cause vvritten, {{sc|This is Iesvs the king of the iewes}}. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=38}}† Then vvere crucified vvith him tvvo theeues: one on the right hand, and one on the left. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=39}}† And they that passed by, blasphemed him, vvagging their heades, {{verse|chapter=27|verse=40}}† and saying, Vah, thou that destroyest the temple of God, and in three daies doest reedifie it: saue thine ovvne self: {{sup|‖}} if thou be the sonne of God, come dovvne from the Crosse. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=41}}† In like maner also the cheefe Priestes With the Scribes and auncients mocking, said: {{verse|chapter=27|verse=42}}† He saued other: him self he can not saue: if he be the King of Israel, let him novv come dovvne from the Crosse, and vve vvil beleeue him. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=43}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 21, 9. Sap. 2, 18.''}}* He trusted in God: let him novv deliuer him if he vvill: for he said, That I am the sonne of God. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=44}}† And the self same thing the theeues also that were crucified vvith him, reproched him vvithal.

{{verse|chapter=27|verse=45}}† And from the sixt houre, there vvas darkenesse made vpon the vvhole earth, vntil the ninthe houre. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=46}}† And about the ninthe houre {{sc|Iesvs}} cried vvith a mighty voice, saying, ''Eli, Eli, lamma-sabacthani''? that is, ''My God, my God, {{sup|‖}} vvhy hast thou forsaken me''? {{verse|chapter=27|verse=47}}† And certaine that stoode there and heard, said, He calleth Elias. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=48}}† And incontinent one of them running, tooke a sponge, & filled it vvith vinegre: and put it on a reede, and gaue him to drinke. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=49}}† And other said, Let be, let vs see vvhether Elias come to deliuer him. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=50}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} againe crying vvith a mighty voice, yelded vp the ghost. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=51}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=HORA NONA in the Churches Seruice.}}And be hold the vele of the temple vvas rent in tvvo peeces, from the toppe euen to the botome. and the earth did quake, and the rockes vvere rent, {{verse|chapter=27|verse=52}}† and the graues vvere opened: and many bodies of the saincts that had slept, rose. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=53}}† And they going forth out of the graues after his resurrection, came into the holy citie: and appeared to many. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=54}}† And the Centurion and they that vvere vvith him vvatching {{sc|Iesvs}}, hauing seen the earth-quake and the things that vvere done, vvere sore afraid, saying, In deede this vvas the sonne of God.

{{verse|chapter=27|verse=55}}† And there vvere there many vvomen a farre of, vvhich had folovved {{sc|Iesvs}} from Galilee, ministring vnto him: {{verse|chapter=27|verse=56}}† among vvhom vvas Marie Magdalene, and Marie the mother of Iames and Ioseph, and the mother of the sonnes of Zebedee. {{verse|chapter=27|verse=57}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=HORA VESPERARVM, or, Euensong.}}And vvhen it vvas euening, there came a certaine<noinclude>{{rh|||rich}}</noinclude>
